meta.title: Ondra Backlog Climb
meta.description: Turns a group backlog into one digest of who said what, when, in which group, and hands it over only in a private chat (handbook §1.5, P2). Four decisions are fixed. First, the summary is not model-written: links are dropped, whitespace is squeezed, and text is cut at a sentence boundary, all deterministically; real summarizing belongs to the dialogue model, and calling a model here would tie latency and cost to every backlog read. Second, nothing is posted into a group: a group backlog is what the owner has not seen, not something to be read back into the group, so a group turn gets an empty plan, which is how "wake only in private" is enforced. Third, not one character of the backlog is written to disk; only the cursor is kept, meaning how far each group has been read and which fingerprints were already seen, and a restart relies on the channel to re-push. Losing one backlog read is better than keeping a corpus nobody agreed to. Fourth, planning is not delivery: sending can fail, so the cursor advances only on an explicit commit, otherwise those messages are never mentioned again and no error is reported. The digest never ends with "N unread" because that is a counter, not a sentence; the folded count stays in logs and panels. This package registers no tools, runs no timers, makes no network requests and draws no interface: backlog comes from the channel adapters, whether to send belongs to the proactive gate, and the digest view belongs to the app shell.
